note: Israel, read on 2026-10-30 on the Ministry of Foreign Affairs' own mission pages (the Consulate General in Los Angeles and the Embassy in London, 'Application for work visa in Israel', last updated 15 June 2026); the Population and Immigration Authority's pages on gov.il answered with a Cloudflare check and weren't read. The B/1 work visa is for a person whose stay is approved for a limited period for work, given to experts and artists among others, including foreign specialists, athletes and performing artists invited to Israel, and only with the Population and Immigration Authority's approval: the employer submits the application, and pays its fee, at one of the Ministry of Interior's population offices in Israel, and on approval the mission in the country where the applicant lives issues the visa after a personal interview (apply kept as abroad, where the person applies; the employer's part is in Israel). It is for one to be paid into an Israeli bank account by an Israeli company; the Spanish Embassy in Tel Aviv adds that, in general, only nationals and permanent residents may take up work or their own business freely, so the work is read as for the sponsor. The fee's amount, the visa's term and decision time aren't stated. Permanent residence and nationality under the Law of Return are for Jews and their families, and non-Jews get stays for study or work only exceptionally and without a path to permanent residence (the Spanish Embassy's summary); no permanent route is written.

sources.title: Consulate General of Israel in Los Angeles, Application for work visa in Israel
sources.said: This visa is also intended for persons eligible under the Law of Return and for foreign specialists, athletes and performing artists who have been invited to Israel ... B/1 Work visa This visa is for a person whose stay in Israel is approved for a limited period of time for the purpose of work. This visa is given to experts and artists, among others, and is granted solely with the approval of Population and Immigration Authority in Israel. The fee is paid by the applicant's employer when the application is submitted to one of the population administration offices of the Ministry of Interior. ... The applicant must present himself for a personal interview at an Israeli mission in the country where he lives.

sources.title: Embassy of Israel in London, Application for work visa in Israel
sources.said: Please note that the application for a work visa is not submitted at the Consulate, but in Israel only and then the approval is sent to our embassy. ... A work visa is granted for a person who wishes to be paid into an Israeli bank account by an Israeli company.

sources.title: Embajada de España en Tel Aviv, Documentación y trámites
sources.said: Los no judíos pueden obtener permiso de estancia en Israel por motivos de estudios o trabajo sólo en casos excepcionales y generalmente por un período de tiempo reducido, sin opción a residencia permanente. En general, sólo los nacionales y los residentes permanentes pueden establecer en Israel relaciones laborales o negocios propios con libertad e independencia y de modo indefinido.
